Budgeted link selection with optcompR

Source: R/integrations.R
select_links.Rd

Chooses which candidate links to add to a graph: at most budget pairs, each node gaining at most max_new_degree new links, maximizing the sum of predicted scores (for example link probabilities from a trained link prediction model). The selection is a 0-1 integer program $$\max_{z \in \{0,1\}^P} \sum_p s_p z_p \quad\text{s.t.}\quad \sum_p z_p \le B,\ \sum_{p \ni v} z_p \le d_v,$$ built and solved with optcompR (HiGHS by default). Pairs with a score at or below min_score are never chosen.

Usage

select_links(pairs, scores, budget, max_new_degree = Inf, min_score = -Inf)

Arguments

pairs

Integer matrix, 2 by P, of candidate node pairs (1-based).

scores

Numeric score per pair.

budget

Maximum number of pairs.

max_new_degree

Maximum new links per node (a scalar or one value per node, indexed by node number).

min_score

Pairs scoring at or below this are excluded.

Value

A list with selected (column indices into pairs), pairs (the selected pairs), objective and status.

Details

This is an optional bridge used after training; integer programs are not differentiable and are not part of any model.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("optcompR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  pairs <- rbind(c(1, 1, 2, 3), c(2, 3, 3, 4))
  select_links(pairs, c(0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6), budget = 3, max_new_degree = 1)
}
#> $selected
#> [1] 1 4
#> 
#> $pairs
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    3
#> [2,]    2    4
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] 1.5
#> 
#> $status
#> [1] "optimal"
#>
